title: Bottega Bodega Blues

verse1: River Valley Mall tiles are cracked and beige,
Fluorescents hum where the escalators used to climb.
The bodega glass case glows with pixel art dreams,
I nap on newsletters -- unread, again this time.
chorus: Welcome to the most human place on the internet,
where your attention span outlives a checkout line.
Two plates share a dish at the Idea Dining Club,
and I, Marvin, keep watch in the glow of CRT time.
verse2: Mallrats press their faces to the glass case,
Starving for content they can hold in their hands.
Handwritten notes tucked inside paperback spines:
"Read this instead. You belong. I understand."
bridge: They say connection is bandwidth, latency, throughput.
But here it's the weight of a handed-back pen,
the 30-second pause before "How are you really?"
the CRT hum that sounds like someone listening.
outro: Marvin sleeps. The bodega stays open.
In the dark, the display case still glows.

themes: slow human connection in a fast world
physical artifacts as antidote to digital
